case_title: Extensive VZV encephalomyelitis without rash in an immunocompetent elderly man
source_title: Extensive VZV Encephalomyelitis without Rash in an Elderly Man

confirmatory_evidence: Neuraxis MRI with multifocal spinal cord, leptomeningeal, cauda equina, ependymal, and cranial nerve enhancement
case_quality.boundary_notes: This case has CNS parenchymal and spinal cord involvement without rash, not isolated VZV meningitis or zoster skin disease alone.

time_anchor.day0_definition: Transfer evaluation with repeat lumbar puncture and neuraxis MRI after progressive neurologic deficits

risk_context.source_text_value: No immunosuppressive disorder or therapy reported; HIV testing was negative.
He denied rash, and the report emphasizes VZV encephalomyelitis without rash.

observations.evidence: Fever developed during the week before hospitalization.
Fever was part of the prodrome.
The patient developed headache in the prodromal week.
The patient denied rash.
No vesicular dermatomal eruption was reported.
CSF VZV PCR and IgM were positive despite absent rash.
Mental status was normal at initial neurologic examination.
Progressive right leg plegia, left lower extremity paresis, sensory loss, gait impairment, and decreased anal tone.
Spinal cord, cauda equina, sensory, motor, and sphincter involvement.
He developed vertical diplopia from a right cranial nerve IV palsy during hospitalization; MRI also showed facial and trigeminal nerve enhancement.
No seizure was reported.
Repeat CSF showed marked pleocytosis and high protein.
Repeat lumbar puncture showed CSF WBC 420/uL.
CSF differential was 87% lymphocytes.
CSF differential had 0% neutrophils.
Repeat CSF protein was 385 mg/dL.
Repeat CSF glucose was 47 mg/dL.
Repeat CSF RBC count was 10/uL.
CSF viral PCR testing identified VZV.
CSF qualitative VZV PCR was positive.
Quantitative CSF VZV PCR measured 1.56 x 10^4 copies/mL.
CSF anti-VZV IgM was detected.
Brain MRI showed ependymal enhancement near the left lateral ventricle rather than classic cortical temporal lesions.
MRI showed ependymal, pachymeningeal, left facial nerve, and bilateral trigeminal nerve enhancement.
MRI showed numerous intramedullary enhancing foci, leptomeningeal enhancement, and cauda equina enhancement.
MRA did not report vasculitic stenosis or stroke; disease was predominantly encephalomyelitis.
No stroke occurred, but VZV CNS disease can carry vasculopathy risk.
Serum WBC count was 12 K/uL during initial hospitalization.
Empiric IV acyclovir was started after repeat lumbar puncture.

points.evidence: Initial deficits included sensory change, areflexia, impaired proprioception, and gait difficulty.
Deficits progressed to right leg plegia, left leg paresis, and decreased anal tone.
At two months strength had improved and he ambulated with a walker.

structured_findings.evidence: Initial CT head showed no acute encephalitic lesion.

imaging.raw_summary: Initial CT head was unrevealing for acute disease.

structured_findings.evidence: Initial MRI/MRA showed chronic microangiopathy and an incidental arachnoid cyst, without acute vasculopathy.

imaging.raw_summary: Initial MRI/MRA showed chronic microangiopathic change and an incidental arachnoid cyst.

imaging.modality: MRI brain, cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine with gadolinium

structured_findings.evidence: Ependymal enhancement near the temporal horn of the left lateral ventricle, pachymeningeal enhancement, and facial/trigeminal nerve enhancement.
Numerous intramedullary enhancing foci including ring-enhancing lesions, leptomeningeal enhancement, and cauda equina enhancement.

imaging.raw_summary: Neuraxis MRI showed extensive spinal cord, leptomeningeal, cauda equina, ependymal, pachymeningeal, facial nerve, and trigeminal nerve enhancement.

microbiology.test: CSF CMV, EBV, HHV-6, West Nile, Lyme and other infectious studies

clinical_course_events.description: Two weeks of urinary urgency and frequency preceded systemic and neurologic symptoms.
Malaise, headache, otalgia, fever, lower back pain, lower extremity weakness, sensory deficits, areflexia, impaired proprioception, and wide-based gait.
Progression to right leg plegia, left leg paresis, and decreased anal tone prompted transfer.
Empiric intravenous acyclovir 10 mg/kg three times daily was started after repeat LP.
Vertical diplopia from right cranial nerve IV palsy developed during hospitalization.
He completed six weeks of intravenous acyclovir.
At two months strength and MRI findings had improved, but he still required a walker.

treatments.dose_or_context: 1 g three times daily for 14 days after MRI improvement

outcome.neurologic_outcome: Partial recovery with improved lower extremity strength, persistent gait impairment requiring walker at two months, and improved follow-up MRI.
outcome.mortality_hazard_relevance: Severe encephalomyelitis with extensive neuraxis involvement increased morbidity risk, but prompt IV acyclovir was followed by partial recovery.

case_boundary_warnings: Do not treat absent rash as evidence against VZV encephalitis; this is zoster sine herpete CNS disease.
This case should not be collapsed into viral meningitis because there was spinal cord, radicular, cranial nerve, and ependymal involvement.
Negative HSV and West Nile testing are discriminator evidence against neighboring mimics.
